Lamashtu (The Wounded Mother).name: Lamashtu (The Wounded Mother)
Lamashtu (The Wounded Mother).description:
Most depictions of Lamashtu depict a horrific entity with abhorrent goals. However, there's a not insignificant number of her worshippers who wonder if this truly is the case. Goblins, kholo, nephelim—people long ascribed to be her unholy spawn—find a certain sympathy in their hearts for them. They see a kinder side to Lamashtu; a Lamashtu who is a safe place for the hunted, who cares for her children regardless of their origin, who bites only because she is protecting her young. These gentler clerics of Lamashtu hope that one day, she can be turned just as Nocticula was. The fact that they still have their divine powers proves that perhaps there's hope after all.

Edicts protect monsters from unfair judgment, aid the impoverished, show pride in your unusual attributes

Anathema put a monster to a needless death, judge others by their appearance, live extravagantly

Areas of Concern the subjugated, childbirth, mercy

Gozreh (The Vast Titans).name: Gozreh (The Vast Titans)
Gozreh (The Vast Titans).description:
Gozreh's image is often used throughout the inner sea by sea monster cults that wish to hide in plain sight; deep one worshippers, shrines to outer gods like Bokrug or demon lords like Dagon. Sometimes, the secret practices and real practices blend into one, and the elusive cult of The Vast Titan arises. These cultists look on in awe at the destructive power of Gozreh, and see creatures like kaiju as their spawn. They see the ocean as a breeding ground for power unlike any other, and seek to see even more power spawn within the deep. Dangerous rituals occur in the dark of the night, with whispers and tests of endurance by way of holding ones' breath for as long as possible. They may pray for the waves to take small villages, to feed the ocean's hunger for destruction. Other worshippers of Gozreh are aware of this sect, but do not persecute them, as they see the cult as a reminder of the sea's dark power.

Edicts Witness natural disasters, pave the way for monster attacks in coastal areas, celebrate large losses of life.

Anathema Act against a kaiju, save someone from drowning, prevent wide scale disasters

Areas of Concern Arial and aquatic megafauna, natural disasters, megalophobia

Nethys (The Broken Mask).name: Nethys (The Broken Mask)
Nethys (The Broken Mask).description:
Some whisper that the greatest secret of Nethys is that his ascension to godhood was not a gift, but a curse that his congregation believes has a hideous truth. Nethys gained power and knowledge of all existence and as such, all questions were answered in the blink of his all seeing eyes. With this came a price and a single question that remained for him to answer: What would there be if nothing, not even the gods, existed? The doomsday cult of The Broken Mask believe that when Nethys ultimately loses control of his balance, it will be the total eradication of all life, knowledge and magic. The void that is left after this final blink will be an empty paradise where they shall live eternally.

Edicts destroy the knowledge of others, disrupt balance and equilibrium, prepare for the end-times

Anathema waste an opportunity to snuff out secrets forever, aid in preserving the cosmic status quo, use your magic to aid others who won't further your plans

Areas of Concern nihilism, secrets, magic

Irori (Purveyor of Perception).name: Irori (Purveyor of Perception)
Irori (Purveyor of Perception).description:
While some see Irori as the seeker of perfection, other’s believe this view is a misreading of his views on perfection and that self-acceptance is the true path to perfection. As a leaf in the wind’s path travels eloquently and without err, so too do these followers of Irori which see experience as the ultimate sculptor of magnificence. Where other followers of the deity might strive for hours on end to master a lesson or art, this sect believes the lessons of life are dealt by the hands of fate instead of claimed by one's own hands. Do not try to control the universe's plans for you; embrace them, and let them take you wherever you are needed! Depictions of Irori within this sect are of a smiling man with unkempt hair at peace with his place in the universe no matter what happens.

Edicts exude confidence; help others find acceptance for themselves; adapt to all aspects of life, no matter how unexpected.

Anathema become too rigid in one's own ideology, refuse to adapt to changes, avoid partaking in new experiences

Areas of Concern adaptation, contentedness, and self acceptance

Urgathoa (The Proscribed Proctor).name: Urgathoa (The Proscribed Proctor)
Urgathoa (The Proscribed Proctor).description:
Though worship of Urgathoa is nearly universally reviled, there exists one particularly unusual group of her followers with equally bizarre teachings— that Urgathoa is the mother of science and medicine. This faith is worshiped openly in Ustalav and Geb, especially among the rich and the academic. They claim that her rebellion against Pharasma was the first act of scientific curiosity, and argue that the undead are an area of academics unjustly decried as immoral. Most notably, these followers have developed strange magic that uses electricity rather than negative energy, which they view as debased. They use this to justify their practices as acceptable, though few recognize their genius.

Edicts learn what others are afraid to learn, create life, document your findings thoroughly

Anathema Allow ethics to sway your decisions, destroy your creations, be imprisoned for your works or beliefs

Areas of Concern academics, experiments, undeath

Special The harm spell loses the void trait for you, and instead gains the electricity trait. It still affects the living and the undead the same way as it normally would.

Abadar (Father Progress).name: Abadar (Father Progress)
Abadar (Father Progress).description:
Some churches of Abadar look not to the past, but to the future—and that future is industry. Firearms, electricity, mechanical boats that can travel the stars; the world of Golarion is at the brink of a revolution, and some believe that in the far future, Abadar will be a patron of invention and technology. Clerics of this type have even begun experimenting with new breeds of commerce: for example, converting churches of Abadar to stores which sell technological innovations branded with his symbol. Whether or not these aspirations to a worldwide Abadar Corporation will come true remains to be seen. However, hotbeds of this denomination in Absalom or Alkenstar certainly try.

Edicts invest in new ideas, create efficient solutions to old problems, sell your inventions

Anathema destroy mechanical objects, allow ancient customs to sway your decision-making, give up on a project before its time.

Areas of Concern technology, invention, branding

Rovagug (The Law-Eater).name: Rovagug (The Law-Eater)
Rovagug (The Law-Eater).description:
The most powerful beasts are the ones that ambush their prey. This is the mantra of the Church of The Law-Eater, a sect of Rovagug that blends into civilization. They understand that the gods only imprisoned Rovagug because they were afraid of his strength, but also understand that Rovagug lost because there was nobody else to fight for him. As such, to do his work properly, you must convince the masses of his goals. This church sneers at the more brutal cults of Rovagug that hide away from society, and instead actively partake in it. They follow strict athletic regimes and influence politics and education to push their ideals. Their ultimate goal is to bring society to its knees through its own laws, highlighting the folly of a world that cares for others.

Edicts Work within the system to cause cruelty and injustice, use subtlety to convince others of your views, eat the hearts of those you have successfully pushed into poverty or prison

Anathema announce your allegiance to Rovagug to someone who won't join you and let them survive, live in the wilderness, use your influence to improve the lives of others

Areas of Concern Politics, heretics, policing

Iomedae (The Wyrmknight).name: Iomedae (The Wyrmknight)
Iomedae (The Wyrmknight).description:
Iomedae is widely renowned as a patron deity to humans… and to some, a patron deity to kobolds. Pointing out her almost impossible victories and bravery that no mere mortal could accomplish, these kobolds claim that Iomedae was never a human, but a empyreal dragon in disguise. They often cite her divine herald, Peace Through Vigilance. This gold dragon refers to his patron as "Mother Iomedae", and rumours have long swirled that he is her offspring, sired by Apsu. How could this be, the kobolds crow, if she herself were not a dragon? There are few dragons in this particular sect, as most find the insinuation amusing at best. However, a number of gold and silver dragons still honour the Wyrmknight for her accomplishments alongside ancients of their kind.

Edicts Protect the meek, show your power in awesome displays in combat, act with humility and respect outside of combat.

Anathema Take credit for your great deeds, disrespect humans or dragons, slay a metallic dragon

Areas of Concern crusades, dragons, justice

Erastil (The Great Elk King).name: Erastil (The Great Elk King)
Erastil (The Great Elk King).description:
Erastil is one of the oldest gods worshipped on Golarion, growing alongside his followers through prehistory and after they left hunter-gathering for farming. However, some sects still worship him in his original form: an elk the size of a mountain with colossal trees for antlers. Legends whisper that The Great Elk helped ward off creatures that would have otherwise hunted his followers with great bugling that shook the air. Some say it was his steps that created thunder, his shed horns that created the trees, and his travels that created valleys between mountains. The Great Elk’s worshippers focus much less on organized worship, instead leaving smaller shrines to the elk god and performing small rituals to ask Erastil for a good hunt, or for safety from dangerous predators that are closing in. Worship of the Great Elk King is most common in wild and forgotten worlds, particularly in the Broken Lands.

Edicts Take in the beauty of nature, use all parts of an animal you've hunted, protect your clan from dangerous predators

Anathema hunt for sport, disturb natural structures, show cowardice in the face of natural threats

Areas of Concern wilderness, ancient traditions, nomads
